title: Environment file: dev, staging, prod
description: One file for each environment, named after it (prod.yaml). Pillars and systems are shared by every environment; this file says what differs.

name.description: Name in the environment picker. Defaults to the file name.

order.description: Where it stands in the picker, lowest first. Ties go by id.

default.description: The environment shown when none is asked for. Without one, the first.

sources.description: Where this environment's numbers come from, by source name. The names metrics and messaging are what the signals use unless a signal says otherwise (see signals); incidents is where open incidents come from. Any other kebab-case name defines a source a signal can be pointed at.

kind.description: The kind of source. A kind may be accepted before the adapter that reads it exists; until then its signals show no data.

connection.description: How to reach it (a workspace, an endpoint). Not used by the fake source.

credential.description: Azure sources only: the login to use, by name from credentials. Without it, the Azure CLI login (az login).

pollSeconds.description: How often the source is asked. Default 30.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one ask may take before it is given up. Default 10.

credentials.description: How Azure sources sign in, by name. A source without a credential uses the Azure CLI login; to change that for all of them, define one called default.

kind.description: azure-cli: whoever az login signed in. default: the Azure SDK's usual chain. managed-identity: the identity of the machine it runs on. service-principal: an app registration.

tenantId.description: The directory to sign in to. Without it, the login's own.

clientId.description: The app registration (service-principal) or user-assigned identity (managed-identity).

clientSecretEnv.description: service-principal only: the name of the environment variable that holds the secret. The secret itself never goes in a registry file.

signals.description: Which source each signal comes from in this environment: a source name from sources, or none. A signal not listed here uses the source called metrics (messaging for backlog and deadLetters). A signal with no source is absent: not shown, not grey.

tenants.description: The tenants of this environment. Each has a database in every system with a tenantPattern.

id.description: Goes into the database name where the tenantPattern has {tenant}.

name.description: What the tenant is called on screen.

kind.description: A test tenant (smoke tests, QA, sandboxes) is drawn paler and striped, can be hidden, and shows amber at worst, never red.

exclude.description: Systems that are not deployed in this environment. They are left out of its town, and an island with no system left is not on the map.

fake.description: Settings for the fake source only.

undeclaredTenants.description: Tenants the fake source finds in the data that the tenants list does not name, so the town can show an unknown tenant.
